correctness.rationale: The source's own definition says a 2-inner-product square vanishes exactly for a linearly dependent pair. For any nonzero a and b, the direct-sum vectors a⊕2b and a⊕b are linearly independent, while both component pairs in formula (10) are dependent, making the proposed square exactly zero. The contradiction is purely algebraic. The comparison repair in the Hilbert-induced subclass is the standard Gram-determinant 2-inner product on the orthogonal Hilbert direct sum.

value.rationale: The direct-sum construction is an advertised final component of the article and is retained in the published version. Its failure occurs at the defining axiom of the ambient space, before any delicate frame bound is considered. The witness works in every nontrivial pair of 2-inner-product spaces and identifies the exact geometric mechanism: independent direct-sum vectors can be componentwise dependent. The canonical Hilbert-induced comparison exposes the missing cross terms and gives a mathematically natural repair of the ambient geometry.
